visuals.title: Which segment is the CC PNL?
visuals.prompt: On this schematic pair, select the segment that represents the CC posterior nipple line.

hotspots.neutralLabel: Segment A on the left schematic, nipple to chest-wall edge
Segment B on the right schematic, nipple to muscle edge
Segment C, curved outer skin contour on the left
Segment D, vertical muscle band only on the right
hotspots.revealLabel: Pectoralis band, not the PNL segment

feedback.a: Correct. On CC, PNL runs from nipple to the posterior (chest-wall) edge of the image.
feedback.b: That is the MLO PNL (nipple to anterior pectoralis).
feedback.c: Skin contour is not the PNL measurement.
feedback.d: The muscle is the MLO landmark the PNL meets; it is not itself the PNL segment.

visuals.explanation: CC PNL = nipple to posterior image edge. MLO PNL = nipple perpendicular to anterior pectoralis. Compare those lengths.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Segments are described by which schematic and which endpoints; names are revealed after answering.

history.note: AI-assisted draft source-checked against cited evidence. Items that teach detailed positioning criteria remain outside the clinically reviewed pool.

visuals.title: Find the pectoralis band on a schematic MLO
visuals.prompt: Select the region that represents the pectoralis muscle band on this schematic MLO.

hotspots.neutralLabel: Region D, center of breast outline

feedback.a: Correct. The upper chest-wall band represents pectoralis on this schematic.
feedback.b: That marker is the nipple, used when judging whether muscle reaches nipple level.
feedback.c: That is the lower contour, not the muscle band.
feedback.d: Central outline is breast tissue, not pectoralis.

visuals.explanation: On MLO schematics, pectoralis is the superior-posterior band along the chest wall. Desirable appearance in cited guidance: convex anterior edge, ideally to nipple level.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Regions described by position only until reveal.

visuals.title: Where does view/laterality go?
visuals.prompt: Select the region where MQSA places view and laterality.

hotspots.neutralLabel: Region A, upper-left near chest wall
Region B, right side near outer contour

feedback.a: Correct. View and laterality belong near the axilla.
feedback.c: Too low; not the axillary region.

visuals.explanation: § 900.12(c)(5) places view and laterality near the axilla without obscuring structures.

visuals.title: Which panel shows displacement?
visuals.prompt: Select the panel that schematically shows implant displacement (tissue drawn forward, implant back).

feedback.a: Left panel shows implant overlapping native tissue.

visuals.explanation: NCI: implants can hide tissue; implant displacement views may be used. Schematics are not mammograms and not a how-to of hand maneuvers.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Panels identified as left/right; technique names revealed after answer.

glossary.definition: Standard mammographic projection with a superior-to-inferior beam path; paired with MLO for routine imaging and accreditation clinical image submission.
Standard angled projection oriented along the pectoralis to include posterior breast tissue and the axillary tail.
A positioning geometry comparison of posterior tissue depth between CC and MLO; cited open guidance says CC PNL should be no more than about 1 cm less than MLO PNL.
Special mammographic technique named by NCI that may be used because implants can hide breast tissue; used in service of maximizing tissue visualization under MQSA unless modified/contraindicated.
Routine views of an asymptomatic patient.
Individualized mammographic examination for clinical signs/symptoms or abnormal screening findings.
